olivia: FYI hitting weird TS + edge behaviour when running the sample worker with the JS SDK. Runtime: 'Cannot use import statement outside a module'. Types also infer as any/unknown.
max: Usually a resolution issue. Which import path?
olivia: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/js-sdk'` in a Cloudflare Worker.
rachel: Two quick checks: package.json exports map (does it have an explicit import -> esm path?) and tsconfig.moduleResolution.
dom: If bundler picks CJS require, runtime breaks in workers. We should provide a worker entrypoint and an explicit "import" export.
olivia: Current tsconfig: module=ESNext, moduleResolution=node.
max: Change moduleResolution to "bundler" (or node16) for esbuild/vite/wrangler. Also add allowSyntheticDefaultImports.
rachel: On types: our d.ts had multiple overloads; the fallback overload returns any/unknown. That collapses inference for generics. We should prefer one generic signature like `call<T = JsonValue>(...): Promise<T>`.
dom: Agreed. Short-term workaround: annotate call sites `await client.call<MyType>(...)` or add a small ambient module declaration in a local .d.ts.
olivia: I patched the sample app: added ./worker export to package.json and switched moduleResolution to bundler. Worker runs, types improved but still needed one call-site generic.
max: For a proper fix: 1) add worker export in published package, 2) change d.ts to single generic signature / change default generic to JsonValue, 3) add typesVersions for compatibility, 4) add CI test that bundles the package for worker target.
rachel: I'll open PRs: types cleanup + worker export + README troubleshooting snippet (edge + tsconfig tips).
bot-ci: CI job #902 failed on edge-integration yesterday, created issue #742 assigned to @eng-runtime.
olivia: Thanks — will update the sample app onboarding with the minimal tsconfig and import path.
